sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate is semantically faithful: it targets ship, uses the declared applicability inputs consistently, applies the inclusive >= 12 nautical-mile threshold with the required quantity datatype and unit, and conditionally requires the distance from an area with nearby ice concentration > 0.1. All dependency-contract terms are represented and deterministic validation is valid.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the applicability logic: arcticWaters is declared as an applicability term and is imposed as a mandatory ship property, but the conditional query ignores it and instead independently tests operatingArea, creating an unused and redundant applicability fact. Use the declared applicability inputs consistently (or remove the redundant arcticWaters obligation if operatingArea is the authoritative selector), and ensure the distance-from-area result is explicitly required only for the applicable ice-concentration-above-one-tenth case, without a disconnected presence-only iceConcentration check.

Preserve the prior applicability repair: the dependency contract declares arcticWaters, operatingArea, and foodWasteDischargeToSea as applicability inputs, but this shape omits arcticWaters and instead independently tests operatingArea, leaving the declared applicability fact unused. Either make the declared inputs consistent and target them correctly on the ship, or explicitly remove the redundant arcticWaters obligation if operatingArea is the authoritative selector. Also bind the recorded distance requirement to the applicable ice-concentration-above-one-tenth condition rather than using a disconnected presence-only distance check; ensure the recorded distance is the distance from the qualifying ice area. The canonical terms are already supplied, so no matcher is needed.

Preserve the prior applicability repair: use the declared arcticWaters, operatingArea, and foodWasteDischargeToSea inputs consistently on the ship. Remove the disconnected iceConcentration property/check, or explicitly connect it to the qualifying nearby ice-concentration operand; the current optional, presence-only iceConcentration constraint does not encode a required relationship. The conditional logic must require the distanceFromAreaWithIceConcentrationAboveOneTenth result specifically for the qualifying area where nearbyIceConcentration > 0.1, not merely accept any recorded distance. Keep the nearest-feature distance comparison inclusive at >= 12 nautical miles and enforce the required quantity structure and units. All needed canonical terms are already supplied; no matcher is needed.

The candidate is semantically faithful: it targets ship, uses the declared applicability inputs consistently, applies the inclusive >= 12 nautical-mile threshold with the required quantity datatype and unit, and conditionally requires the distance from an area with nearby ice concentration > 0.1. All dependency-contract terms are represented and deterministic validation is valid.
